articles.fullText:
The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting was held in Shenzhen on November 18-19. Following Shanghai and Beijing, Shenzhen became the third Chinese city to host an APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. Its openness, connectivity and innovation-driven dynamism reflect the resilience and vitality of Asia-Pacific cooperation.
APEC’s economic and trade connectivity has continued to deepen. In the first ten months of 2026, China’s trade in goods with other APEC economies reached 27.08 trillion yuan, up 25.4 percent year on year. Since 2026, the Port of Shenzhen has opened 30 new shipping routes passing through APEC economies, further densifying the Asia-Pacific shipping network. In July, Port of Shenzhen signed the APEC Economies Port Friendship Cooperation Agreement with 16 ports across 10 APEC economies. Denser routes and better-connected ports have made the gains of Asia-Pacific cooperation increasingly tangible.
Green transition in 2026 has moved faster from vision to rules and action. The 16th APEC Energy Ministerial Meeting in Beijing in September proposed and systematically defined the “Asia-Pacific Energy Community” for the first time. The Shenzhen Initiative, adopted at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 in November, further called for accelerating the establishment of a green trade rules framework, promoting the shift toward zero- and low-carbon mobility, and safeguarding stable, resilient and smooth flows in green supply chains—extending green rules from the energy production end to the trade and supply chain end. The APEC meetings themselves became a demonstration of green transition: key venues, transport hubs and reception facilities ran on 100 percent green electricity. Asia-Pacific green transition is thus acquiring a verifiable pace of implementation in 2026.
Frontier fields such as new energy and artificial intelligence have become key drivers of global development and important agenda items for Asia-Pacific cooperation. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 “building an open and inclusive AI innovation ecosystem” as one of its seven sub-themes, grounding technological cooperation in the scale of inclusive sharing. Digital and smart economic and trade cooperation has become the area with the broadest consensus and strongest cooperative atmosphere among APEC members. At the APEC CEO Summit, Chinese and foreign participants held in-depth exchanges on trade digitalization, AI, digital services and other topics, exploring ways to accelerate the application of innovations and deeper industrial integration.
From shipping routes and clean energy to industrial collaboration and smart technologies, cooperation across the Asia-Pacific is advancing through concrete actions and shared achievements.
APEC is not a game for a select few economies to lead. It is a shared endeavor in which all members contribute to building capacity and fostering a stronger regional ecosystem. Through openness, innovation and cooperation, the Asia-Pacific community continues to move forward, strengthened by closer connections and shared opportunities.

articles.fullText:
Record rainfall, surging waves and vulnerable seawalls are only a foretaste of what's to come, scientists warn, as El Niño-driven sea level rise and "king tides" threaten California's shoreline this week.
Early Thursday, the US National Weather Service warned California's coastal residents of approaching storms, reporting rainfall rates exceeding 25.4 mm per hour and issuing multiple flash flood warnings.
Coastal and nature preserve trails around Point Vicente and Pelican Cove Park remain closed after heavy rains and dangerous conditions in Rancho Palos Verdes, California, the US, November 21, 2026. 
An atmospheric river, fueled by the super El Niño, caused flooding in San Francisco on Wednesday, dumping about 67 mm of rain in one day and surpassing a record for that date that has stood for over a hundred years. Floodwaters inundated buildings and stranded cars on bay area freeways, and more than 51,000 electricity customers were left without power by Wednesday afternoon.
El Niño, a climate pattern marked by warmer-than-normal waters in the tropical Pacific, can bring wetter and stormier conditions to California. It can also temporarily raise sea levels along the US West Coast, allowing high tides and powerful waves to reach farther inland than usual.
Large swells continued to batter Southern California's coast on Thursday, worsening erosion and damage from earlier storms. In October, a 110-meter crack appeared in a coastal bluff beneath Pacific Coast Highway near Crystal Cove State Park, prompting Caltrans to restrict traffic to one lane in each direction while crews worked to stabilize the slope.
A boat is seen offshore as a "king tide" is expected to peak along the Southern California coast in Rancho Palos Verdes, California, the US, November 21, 2026. 
Scientists expect the true test next week, when unusually high "king tides" run from Sunday through November 27, potentially accompanied by large swells and further rain. Starting Monday, coastal water levels in parts of Southern California could reach up to 2.4 meters.
According to the California Coastal Commission, the season's highest tides won't even hit until November 24-26, December 23-25 and January 21-22.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration estimates roughly a 60% probability, for October through December at minimum, of a "historic" El Niño, one that would exceed every event since records began in 1950.
California is stepping up efforts to protect its coastal infrastructure. California Governor Gavin Newsom, who declared a statewide state of emergency on September 21, signed an executive order on October 27 establishing a Highway 1 Task Force to identify vulnerable sections of the coastal highway and accelerate preventive work.
According to the governor's office, emergency project expenditures along the Big Sur section of Highway 1 totaled about $312 million from 2020 through 2026.

articles.title: What a historic trilateral meeting means to the world
articles.titleCn: 历史性的三边会晤对世界意味着什么
articles.summary: The China-Russia-US trilateral meeting sends a positive signal to the world and carries significant implications for the regional and broader global community, international experts say.

paragraphs.en: The China-Russia-US {{1}} meeting sends a positive signal to the world and carries significant {{2}} for the {{3}} and broader global community, international experts say. The meeting, which took place on Thursday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, marked a {{0}} first, with the leaders of the three countries sitting down together for direct talks. articles.fullText:
The China-Russia-US trilateral meeting sends a positive signal to the world and carries significant implications for the regional and broader global community, international experts say.
The meeting, which took place on Thursday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, marked a historic first, with the leaders of the three countries sitting down together for direct talks.
Alexey Maslov, director of the Institute of Asian and African Studies, noted that the meeting is an encouraging sign, as it demonstrates that the leaders of China, Russia and the United States are both willing and able to engage in dialogue.
While differences among the three countries remain, Maslov stressed that what matters most is their ability to listen to each other and communicate.
Following the meeting, the three leaders jointly issued the "China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace," with the title itself reflecting the shared aspirations of the three countries.
Zamir Awan, the founding chair of the Global Silk Route Research Alliance, called the meeting "successful" and highlighted its significance to the international community, as it addresses issues that affect the common interests of all humanity.
Stressing the value of the occasion, Sourabh Gupta, a senior research fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies (ICAS) in Washington, DC, emphasized that major countries need to come together at the negotiating table to establish basic principles and boundaries, as these are essential to building a stable global system.
Carlos Aquino Rodriguez, director of the Center for Asian Studies (CEAS) and a professor in the Faculty of Economic Sciences at the National University of San Marcos in Peru, said the meeting can help prevent conflicts among major countries while also contributing to the resolution of regional issues, which is what the international community broadly hopes to see.
"I believe cooperation is essential to resolving conflicts. What the world needs is certainty, coordination and cooperation," Rodriguez added.

articles.fullText:
Nvidia's board of directors is meeting on Wednesday to decide whether to remove co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, amid uncertainty over the leadership of the world's leading supplier of AI processors, according to the Wall Street Journal.
Co-founder, president and CEO of Nvidia Jensen Huang speaks during the Nvidia GTC Berlin 2026 Artificial Intelligence conference, Germany, October 21, 2026. 
The meeting follows Nvidia's announcement on November 8 that it had launched an independent investigation into Huang. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside legal counsel, is overseeing the inquiry.
Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 with Curtis Priem and Chris Malachowsky. Over more than three decades at the helm, he has led the company's transformation from a maker of graphics chips for computer games into the world's leading supplier of AI processors. Nvidia is currently valued at around $4 trillion.
According to the company's fiscal 2026 annual filing, Huang beneficially owns approximately 870.6 million shares, representing 3.58% of Nvidia, valued at about $162.5 billion based on the stock's November 6 closing price. Approximately 800.9 million of those shares, worth about $149.5 billion at the same price, are held through trusts, limited liability companies and a family foundation involving both Huang and his wife, Lori Huang. The couple share trustee, voting or investment responsibilities in several of these arrangements.
No obvious successor has been identified, raising questions about leadership continuity should Huang depart. Nvidia shares fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday.

articles.fullText:
China's longest carbon dioxide transmission pipeline was put into operation in northeast China's Jilin Province, China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) said on Monday.
The Jilin Petrochemical-Jilin Oilfield pipeline, measuring 277.6 kilometers in length, can transport up to 3.3 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually. It boasts the country's largest diameter, highest pressure and the largest designed transportation capacity of its kind.
The trunk line crosses three cities in Jilin Province – Jilin, Changchun and Songyuan, and connects the carbon capture facilities at Jilin Petrochemical upstream with oil recovery and carbon storage operations at Jilin Oilfield downstream.
During construction, engineers made a series of technological breakthroughs and achieved the domestic production of several key pieces of equipment.
Ma Xiaohong, chief expert at Jilin Oilfield, said wind and solar power are being used to supply green electricity to the project, helping reduce carbon emissions throughout its lifecycle.
CNPC is now using the pipeline as the backbone of a regional carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) network. The supporting carbon dioxide recovery project at Jilin Petrochemical, with an annual capacity of 800,000 tonnes, went fully into operation in October, providing a stable supply to the pipeline.
